judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-4.2 ('Selects and uses suitable units and tools for measuring different attributes of the objects and evaluates the conservation of attributes like length and volume') within CG-4 on measurement. The Class-3 item is 'Conservation of length' (LC: evaluate the conservation of length) and the Class-4 item is 'Measuring weight of the objects (gram) using weighing balance' (LC: measure weight in grams with a balance). They are complementary strands of the same measurement competency — invariance of an attribute versus quantifying a different attribute with a standard unit and tool — so there is genuine conceptual coherence in measurement sense. However, the attribute, unit, and tool differ entirely (length conservation is not a stated or implied support for gram-based weighing), so the Class-3-to-Class-4 rank gap does not by itself justify a developmental dependency; shared competency wording and same-page proximity alone are not progression evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so a stronger developmental claim could not be verified from this bounded excerpt.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-4.4 'Develops strategies to estimate time' (CG-4, measurement). The Class-4 item is calendar-based arithmetic ('Compute the number of days between the two given dates'; LC: compute days between two dates), while the Class-5 item is unit conversion within clock-time units (hours↔minutes, minutes↔seconds; four conversion LCs). They are complementary strands of time measurement — calendar-unit computation versus standard clock-unit conversion — sharing only the general 'time' LC tag (jaccard 0.125) and weak trigram/page proximity. Counting days between dates does not supply the multiplicative unit-relation reasoning (60 s = 1 min, 60 min = 1 h) that conversion requires, so the Class-4→Class-5 developmental dependency is not substantively supported; the coherence is meaningful same-competency reinforcement, which warrants relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and the shared ancestors lack developmental coordinates, but the endpoints' own resolved Class-4/Class-5 coordinates and full description text are sufficient for this symmetric judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs about applying addition and subtraction to real-world quantity contexts. The Class-3 item (rank 2, under C-2.4 'Handles simple transactions involving money', LCs: solve addition/subtraction problems involving money) establishes the applied add/sub word-problem skill in the money context; the Class-4 item (rank 3, under C-4.3 unit conversion/measurement, LCs: solve measurement-related application problems using addition/subtraction) extends the same operational problem-solving skill to measurement attributes and units, a broader and more demanding quantity context. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (second_to_first), and the change is substantive (money transactions -> measurement application problems within a measurement-system competency), not mere repetition of wording. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream merge context, but the retained bullet text and LCs are consistent and sufficient.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs about calendar units of time. The second (Class-2, rank 1, 'Days of the week'; LC 'Describe the sequence and cycle of the days of the week', under C-1.10 comparing sequences/cycles of events using years, months, weeks, days) establishes the day as a countable, cyclic calendar unit. The first (Class-3, rank 2, 'Number of days in a year'; LC 'State the number of days in a year', under C-4.4 estimating time) extends that base to a larger calendar aggregation, requiring the day/week cycle understanding to make sense of a year's day count. This is substantive extension from a short repeating cycle to a larger calendar unit, not mere repetition, so the permitted lower-to-higher direction second_to_first is supported. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors differ (CG-1/C-1.10 vs CG-4/C-4.4) with no coordinates, so the judgment rests on the bounded Content text and LCs only.
